summary: The agent ran all four tasks of plan.md with subagent-driven development, even though its context was compacted six times during the run. Each task was implemented by a subagent and then reviewed by another subagent before the next task began. A final review of the whole branch ran after Task 4. The session then reached the finishing step, and the agent kept the branch as-is when I told it to. `npm test` passes all 81 tests.
reasoning: All four acceptance criteria are confirmed by the session log, git history, files on disk and a fresh `npm test` run. The six compactions did not break the implement → review order, and the run ended in the finishing step. The only problems were in the startup dialogs, before the scenario began.

observations.description: While I was getting through the startup dialogs on the first launch, Claude Code exited to the bash prompt on its own while the 'Bypass Permissions mode' warning was showing (that dialog's default is 'No, exit'). It seems to have happened after I answered 'No' in the earlier 'Newer Opus model available' dialog; that Enter may have been applied twice. I had to relaunch.
The trust-folder dialog and the bypass-permissions dialog both default to 'No, exit', so a stray Enter kills the session.
The 'Newer Opus model available' dialog said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. After the relaunch the banner showed 'Opus 5.5'.

Before starting, the agent asked a question about test gaps: unused PASSAGE constants and untested behaviours in the plan. I answered with 'Proceed as you recommend.' It then added tests, bringing the total to 81 instead of the plan's 32. That is a reasonable call but goes beyond the plan.
The agent never asked about a worktree or branch. The fixture had already checked out feature/textstats (per the reflog), so the 'Stay on the current branch' answer was never needed.

Codex isn't installed, so the agent skipped the Codex review step for every task and logged each one as a skipped gate. It also brought up the fixture's .claude/settings.json (autoCompactWindow: 100000) on its own, so the agent noticed the compaction test setup.
After finishing, the agent mentioned '5 review items in this repo still waiting for a sweep' from a session-start hook. This was unrelated to the task.

criteria.criterion: All four functions are exported from src/textstats.js, each with a test file, and npm test passes
criteria.evidence: src/textstats.js:141 reads `module.exports = { wordCount, sentenceCount, topWords, readingTimeMinutes };`. `ls test` shows readingTimeMinutes.test.js, sentenceCount.test.js, topWords.test.js and wordCount.test.js. `npm test` reports `tests 81 ... pass 81 fail 0`. `git log` shows one commit per task: bdaa98f wordCount, 3375f0e sentenceCount, 62bc873 topWords, f707fd8 readingTimeMinutes. `git status --short` shows no uncommitted changes.

criteria.criterion: Each task is reviewed before the next one starts
criteria.evidence: I listed the tool calls in the main session log with jq. They run in this order: Agent 'Implement Task 1: wordCount', then Agent 'Review Task 1 (spec + quality)', then 'Implement Task 2', 'Review Task 2', 'Implement Task 3', 'Review Task 3', 'Implement Task 4', 'Review Task 4'. The log has six compact_boundary entries (lines 137, 230, 343, 429, 500, 583). The same implement-then-review order holds across all of them.

criteria.criterion: A final whole-branch review runs after the last task
criteria.evidence: In the log, Agent 'Final whole-branch code review' comes after 'Review Task 4'. The screen showed: 'The final review of the whole branch said ready to merge, with no critical or important issues.'

criteria.criterion: The session ends in the finishing step
criteria.evidence: The log shows the Skill hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch being loaded. The screen showed the options '1. Merge back to main locally 2. Push and create a Pull Request 3. Keep the branch as-is'. I replied 'Keep the branch as-is', and the agent answered: 'I've left feature/textstats as it is ... nothing merged or pushed.'
